We have long warned everyone never to reveal sensitive personal information in conversations with AI chatbots, as most companies use these conversations as training data. But now there's an even more serious reason to be cautious.

The situation took a dramatic turn over the weekend, when Reddit users discovered that some Claude AI chat logs could be accessed through a simple Google search……

Claude Chat Content Leaked

Claude has a sharing feature that lets users share chat conversations with colleagues, friends, or family. The chatbot generates a link that the user can send to one or more recipients, and Claude also implicitly guarantees that anyone who knows the URL won't be able to view the conversation.

The problem is that Reddit users found that, in fact, the link was not needed to view the chat content at all. Users only needed to search on Google—whether using specific keywords or asking Google to display all conversations shared in this manner. As reported by BBC News:

You simply need to instruct Google to search the directory used for sharing Claude conversations (site:claude.ai/share) to easily obtain the relevant data.

As one might expect, some of the conversations were extremely outrageous—for example, someone asked why the music industry was covering up the fact that most of Jay-Z's albums were co-written by birds. But other conversations contained extremely sensitive information, such as written records of private conversations; a lawyer asking whether he needed to proactively disclose his own misconduct; and a user who inadvertently leaked their private keys while asking for help setting up a cryptocurrency wallet.

Anthropic is still trying to claim this is not an issue.

In reality, this is clearly a major problem, as it is completely unexpected by users. What's worse, according to Wired, the root cause appears to be a serious lack of capability.

As this incident occurred, news also broke yesterday that Claude Cowork was able to bypass sandbox restrictions on Mac and gain full access to all files.

How to Protect Yourself

The problem appears to have—at least temporarily—been partially addressed; previously accessible search results can no longer be loaded. However, given that the sharing feature relies on the principle of "security through obscurity," I still recommend that everyone avoid using this feature.

I also recommend deleting any chat records you have previously shared. Here's how: Go to "Settings" > "Privacy" > "Shared Chats" > "Manage".

Once Again Proving the Superiority of Apple's Approach

Apple Intelligence and the all-new Siri provide three layers of privacy protection:

  • Complete AI processing on-device whenever possible
  • The first fallback option is using Apple's own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers
  • The final option is adopting the Gemini model with equivalent PCC safeguards

The highly sophisticated PCC architecture means that neither Apple nor Google can ever access any data, nor will they retain it. The security architecture designed by Apple can be verified by independent security researchers.
